question: Should `policy watch --interval-ms` continue accepting equivalent base-10 integer spellings such as `+500` and `0500`, or become a canonical unsigned-decimal-only interface?
rationale: The aliases resolve to the same cadence, and neither current documentation nor the shared integer parser establishes canonical spelling as the Policy command contract, so rejecting them is a compatibility and product-policy choice rather than an unambiguous bug fix.

options.title: Preserve current syntax
options.body: Keep equivalent base-10 spellings accepted and close or redesign this PR because no incorrect polling cadence is demonstrated.

options.title: Require canonical decimals
options.body: Explicitly approve the breaking lexical restriction, update the public command documentation, and require supported-Node before/after/control CLI proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve current syntax
recommendation.body: Keep equivalent base-10 spellings accepted and close or redesign this PR because no incorrect polling cadence is demonstrated.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced and shaped the Policy CLI whose accepted-input contract is being changed.
